_readme: THE PLANNING SHAPE VOCABULARY (DRE-2843). One file, read by everything.
A shape answers *how is this work structured, and what gate does it owe*.
Planning treats every card the same today — a full plan artifact, and a
stop for a green light — because there was no way to say 'this one is a
one-liner' or 'this one is a whole wave' anywhere a machine could read.
Per shape: what it means, the LANE a card of that shape goes to, the ACTOR
accountable for it there, whether the sweep may promote it, and the marks
the stamp applies. That is deliberately the same structure as
config/routing-verdicts.json, not a second one: destination and actor are
both drawn from config/lane-contract.json, so a shape naming a lane that
does not exist, or an actor that is not a permitted writer OF THAT LANE,
fails its own check instead of becoming a dead end. OPERATOR and WORKBENCH
shipped without that binding and sent cards to a turn that never came
(DRE-2735); PARKED named `operator` on `Backlog`, a lane whose writers are
all process (DRE-2824). Both were data, and a check like this one is what
found them.
SHAPE IS NOT SIZE, AND THE NEXT READER MUST NOT MERGE THEM.
`size:XS` through `size:XL` already exist and mean EFFORT — how much work
this is. One-off / epic / wave is a different axis: how the work is
STRUCTURED and what gate it owes. A `size:L` one-off is perfectly
legitimate — a large single card that still ships in one pull request and
still needs no green light. Reusing the `size:` prefix would put two
questions behind one word, which is exactly the naming failure the
Plan/Entitlement rule exists to prevent (DRE-1494, and
adr-tenant-plan-vs-llm-billing-naming.md in agent-bureau). So the axes stay
apart mechanically, not by good intentions: a shape named with the `size:`
prefix, or a shape whose marks apply a `size:` label, is refused by
scripts/planning_shape.py check.
Exactly one shape is stamped on a card. A card carrying two is refused
with both named, because picking between them would be inventing the
decision rather than reading it. A card carrying NONE and a card carrying
an unrecognised word are different faults with different messages: the
first has not been classified yet, the second was classified into a
vocabulary that does not exist.
JSON, not YAML: the reader is imported on a product repo's agent job,
where there is no pip install and PyYAML is not guaranteed.
Check this file against the lane contract:
python3 scripts/planning_shape.py check

shapes.name: one-off
shapes.means: One card, one pull request. It owes no plan artifact and stops for no green light.
shapes.why: The most common thing anyone files, and the whole reason the vocabulary exists: a one-liner that is made to owe an epic's paperwork is a planner run and a CEO decision spent on nothing. It lands in Backlog carrying its routing verdict, and the sweep promotes it from there — which is why this is the one shape that is promotable, and why the actor is the sweep that performs the move. Nothing escalates it BY DESIGN, so its verdict is its approval (DRE-2735).

shapes.name: epic
shapes.means: A set of cards that ship separately under one parent, with a plan the CEO approves before any of them run.
shapes.why: The plan artifact and the green light are what an epic owes, and Green Light is the CEO's `needs you` queue where that decision is made — the epic waits there until a human moves it, and its children inherit that approval. The sweep must never promote it: `agent:planner` is the existing label that already stops `reconcile.promote_ready`, so the stamp applies that rather than inventing a second signal (the same reuse WORKBENCH makes of `hand-built`).

shapes.name: wave
shapes.means: A programme of epics — too big for one plan, so what it owes first is a decomposition into epics.
shapes.why: A wave cannot be green-lit as one plan, because the thing a CEO would be approving is not written yet: the first work it owes is being split into epics, and Planning is the lane that owes a decomposition. So it goes to the planner, not to the CEO — asking for approval of a wave-sized card is asking someone to approve a title. Marked `agent:planner` for the same reason an epic is: nothing dispatched builds a container.
